title: Community action on liveability
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:45Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: None of the bank points teach residents getting involved in improving their own area; the closest, Strategies to improve liveability, covers only council-run infrastructure and services, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Community action on liveability
card: Community action is when local people take part in improving the place where they live. It can be started by residents, community groups, schools or the local council.
a shared space where neighbours grow food and plants together. It can give people fresh food, a green space and a place to meet.
an event where volunteers collect rubbish from a park, beach or street. It can make the area cleaner and more pleasant to use.
A youth space is a place made for young people to meet and play. In a council consultation, the council asks residents for their views before it decides on a change.
draft.remember: Community action gets local people involved in improving their own area.

a.q: A council asks residents for their views on a new skate park before it decides where to build it. What is this an example of?
a.why: The council is asking residents for their views before making a decision, which is a council consultation. A youth space is a place for young people, and a skate park may become one, but asking for views is the consultation step.
a.clue: Look at what the council is doing before it decides.

b.q: Residents of a street in Penrith have a vacant lot covered in weeds. They agree to turn it into a shared space where neighbours grow vegetables. Which initiative is this?
b.why: Neighbours working together to grow food and plants on shared land is a community garden. A clean-up day only collects rubbish and does not set up a lasting growing space.
b.clue: What are the neighbours planning to grow?
